summary: This document lists requirements for Ethernet VPN, driven by new uses such as data center interconnect and needs the current VPLS solution does not readily address, like all-active multihoming.

eli5.summary: Old private-network services could not handle some modern needs. This lists what a better design must do.

subtitle: What a better Ethernet VPN has to do that VPLS cannot: all-active multihoming, easier setup and smarter multicast.

tldr.problem: Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS) is widely deployed, but it cannot do all-active multihoming, cannot use Multipoint-to-Multipoint LSPs for multicast, and needs operators to configure many network parameters by hand.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC does not define a protocol. It lists numbered requirements (R1a to R14) that an Ethernet VPN (EVPN) solution must or should meet, grouped as redundancy, multicast, provisioning, service interfaces, convergence, flood suppression, topologies and security.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational requirements document that sets the target for the EVPN solution; it specifies no wire format of its own.

today: RFC 7209 is an Informational requirements document with no listed obsoleting or updating RFC. It does not define a protocol; it states the requirements the EVPN solution was to meet.

sections.title: Why VPLS Is Not Enough
sections.content:
VPLS is described as a proven and widely deployed technology, but the RFC names several limits. Current VPLS supports multihoming only in single-active mode, where one provider edge (PE) router forwards for a given VLAN. It cannot do all-active mode, where every PE in the redundancy group can forward.

For multicast, RFC 7117 uses Point-to-Multipoint (P2MP) LSPs only; there is no defined way to use Multipoint-to-Multipoint (MP2MP) LSPs with VPLS. Provisioning is also heavy: even with BGP auto-discovery, operators must configure network-side parameters on top of the access configuration.

New pressures add to this: data-center interconnect needs a hybrid service called VLAN-aware bundling, virtualization raises the number of MAC addresses, and operators want less flooding and more flexible VPN topologies.
sections.eli5: The old system works, but it can only use one road at a time, needs lots of hand setup, and gets muddled when there are many more cars.

sections.title: Redundancy Requirements
sections.content:
The largest block of requirements covers multihoming a customer edge (CE) device to several PEs. Two modes are defined: single-active (only one PE per VLAN forwards) and all-active (all PEs in the group can forward).

  • R1a/R1b: a solution MUST support flexible flow-based load balancing from the CE, and in the direction toward the CE across all its links, however many PEs it is connected to.
  • R2a/R2b: it MUST use all LSPs and all equal-cost paths between a remote PE and the PEs in the group. The RFC's example has CE1 on PE1 and PE2, CE2 on PE3 and PE4, and three ECMP paths each, giving twelve paths.
  • R3a to R3d: it MUST work without a dedicated link between the PEs, with different IGP costs, and across IGP domains in one Autonomous System; it SHOULD work across multiple Autonomous Systems.
  • R4: it SHOULD forward unicast optimally, meaning traffic is not sent between PEs of a multihomed group unless the destination CE is attached to one of them.
  • R5: it SHOULD allow arbitrary redundancy groups, so one PE can be in several groups at once.
  • R6a to R6d: a multihomed Ethernet network (for example one running MSTP or G.8032) MUST be supported in single-active mode; all-active mode with MAC-based load balancing is only a MAY.
sections.eli5: If your house has two driveways, the new system should let cars use both at once, even if the driveways are in different towns, and should not send cars around the block for no reason.

sections.title: Multicast and Provisioning Requirements
sections.content:
For multicast, broadcast and unknown unicast traffic, MP2MP LSPs can reduce the multicast state held in core routers. RFC 7117 rules them out because VPLS makes the egress PE learn MAC addresses from the sender, and an MP2MP LSP has no inherent way to identify the sender. So a solution MUST provide a mechanism that needs no MAC learning against LSPs on MP2MP (R7a) and SHOULD be able to use MP2MP LSPs for this traffic (R7b).

For provisioning, R8a to R8f ask for auto-discovery of VPN member PEs (MUST) and, as SHOULDs, auto-discovery of redundancy group members, auto-sensing of the site ID with an auto-generated redundancy group ID, and automated Designated Forwarder (DF) election that divides service instances among PEs. Where VLAN identifiers are global (at most 4K services), MPLS and BGP attributes such as the VPN ID and Route Target SHOULD be derived from the VLAN identifier. Defaults SHOULD be used for anything not configured.
sections.eli5: The new system should be able to send one announcement to many people without needing to know who sent each reply, and it should mostly set itself up.

sections.title: Service Interfaces, Convergence and Flooding
sections.content:
The three existing service types are port mode, VLAN mode and VLAN bundling, and a solution MUST support all three (R9a). A fourth, VLAN-aware bundling, puts many customer VLANs into one L2VPN service instance while keeping data-plane separation, with a dedicated bridge domain per VLAN. It comes with or without VLAN ID translation, and a solution MAY support it (R9b).

On failure, recovery from PE-CE circuit and PE node failures MUST be provided, and convergence time MUST be independent of the number of MAC addresses learned (R10a, R10b); it SHOULD also be independent of the number of service instances.

For flooding, operators SHOULD be able to choose per service instance whether unknown unicast is dropped or flooded. For data-center interconnect, broadcast flooding outside a site SHOULD be minimized, especially periodic ARP traffic (R11a to R11c).
sections.eli5: The new system should offer the same kinds of connections as before plus a new one for data centers, bounce back from breakage quickly, and not shout every message to everybody.

sections.title: Topologies, Policies and Security
sections.content:
A solution MUST support flexible VPN topologies (R12a), including E-Tree, where root sites can talk to roots and leaves while leaves can talk only to roots. It MAY support policies per MAC address (R12b) and MUST support inter-AS option-B and option-C scenarios (R12c).

On security, any protocol extensions MUST include a proper security analysis. Two extra requirements are added: a solution MUST detect and handle the same MAC address appearing behind two Ethernet segments, whether inadvertent or malicious (R13), and MUST be able to bind a MAC address to one Ethernet segment, a "sticky MAC". For sticky MACs, mobility is disallowed and traffic for that MAC from other segments MUST be discarded (R14).
sections.eli5: The new system should let some sites only talk to a hub, and it should stop someone from pretending to be another computer by claiming its address.
